faq.headline: Insurance Agency Website FAQs
faq.description: Answers to help you plan a useful website for your agency and its clients.

items.question: How do I create a website for an insurance agency?
items.answer: Start with your agency details, service area, agent profiles, coverage lines, and a clear way for visitors to contact your team. Organize information around the questions clients ask before speaking with an agent.

items.question: Can I explain different types of insurance on my website?
items.answer: Yes. Create pages for the coverage your agency offers, such as home, auto, life, or business insurance. Have your team review the wording so it matches current products and carrier requirements.

items.question: Can visitors request an insurance quote online?
items.answer: Yes. A quote request form can collect basic contact and coverage details so an agent can follow up. A request does not confirm eligibility, a rate, or active coverage.

items.question: Can I publish insurance rates on my website?
items.answer: Only publish rates or examples approved for your products, locations, and agency. Premiums and eligibility can depend on individual details, carrier rules, and applicable regulations.

items.question: Can clients report a claim through my agency website?
items.answer: You can explain how to reach your agency and link to the appropriate insurer claims resources. Make clear which steps are handled by your agency and which are handled by the carrier.

items.question: Can independent insurance agents use this website builder?
items.answer: Yes. Use your site to introduce your agency, explain the coverage you offer, show your service area, and help people start a conversation with an agent.
